source.title: Physics-Informed ML Diagnostic Engine: DXC'26 LiU-ICE Track Solution
source.venue: 37th International Conference on Principles of Diagnosis and Resilient Systems (DX 2026)

method.summary: Recurrent LSTM with physical hidden states; predict rates/directions rather than direct physical values; structurally derived MSO residuals and four virtual sensors; fault diagnosis matrix, fixed alarm thresholds and scalar-product isolation; selective fault-data training after structural decoupling; adaptive covariate-shift compensation.
operational_features: 90 second (1800 sample) initialization/warm-up for covariate adaptation
fixed alarm thresholds over transformed physical residuals
four virtual sensors with two neural networks per sensor
structural model/measurement-set analysis for residual independence and fault isolation
disclosed_limitations: The 0.75 second debounce reduces spike-related false alarms but adds activation delay.
The 90 second adaptation warm-up temporarily reduces sensitivity and creates a blind interval.
A fault present at startup may be assimilated into the healthy baseline during warm-up.
A -10% intake-manifold pressure fault under standard FTP75 produced TDR 21.12%, though the same magnitude was detected under FTP75 Highway.
A +8% intercooler pressure fault under WLTP produced FIA 0.00% alongside a high false-alarm rate.
Air-mass-flow sensor faults were a significant sensitivity challenge.

official_results.metric_identity: The paper's Table 7 explicitly labels the current official components TDR, 1-FAR, FIA and Score. The overall score 88.01 is their arithmetic mean. Do not substitute the older 2024 paper's top-ranked TIR for FIA.

matched_reproduction.protocol: Reproduce the paper's exact 2026 training/evaluation splits, signal selection, state-space design, preprocessing, virtual sensors, fixed thresholds, debounce, adaptation warm-up, training schedule, and class probability interface before modifying the method.
required_recovered_artifacts: fixed class ordering and FIA calculation
matched_reproduction.benchmark_comparability: Published official hidden-test results are a strong external reference, but exact matched re-evaluation on the same public split is needed for a fair architecture comparison.

research_opportunities: Fault-at-startup falsification: inject a labeled fault at sample zero and test whether warm-up adaptation assimilates it as normal.
Dual-track adaptation: keep the certified reference frozen while collecting a quarantined shadow baseline; never let the candidate update the live baseline before independent review.
Regime-specific uncertainty sets: use multi-hypothesis behavioral envelopes and abstain where sensor/condition shift makes fault signatures overlap.
Selective debounce: measure detection delay and FAR jointly; use sequential evidence rather than a fixed 15-sample inertial filter when the data supports faster safe confirmation.
Weak-magnitude isolation: prioritize f_pim(-10%), f_waf(-12%) and f_pic(+8%) stress cells; high aggregate score conceals severe condition-specific failures.
claim_ceiling: Published benchmark reference only. The method and reported scores have not been independently reproduced by Symtropy; the values are not Symtropy results.
